title: Serving Runtime: Architecture, Kernel Scheduling, Profiling & Ops Playbook
author: Aisha Kumar
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the serving-runtime team’s production-facing documentation: architecture overview, kernel scheduling design, profiling and benchmarking playbooks, recent release notes, known issues, and operational runbooks. It is intended for engineers owning the inference runtime, SREs supporting GPU fleets, and on-call responders.

1. Runtime architecture summary

- Purpose: high-throughput, low-latency transformer inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- High-level components:
  - Frontend API Router: auth, rate limit, per-route routing policies (latency/cost/region).
  - Request Router & Broker: performs model routing, batch construction, and KV-cache lookup.
  - Worker Runtime (per-GPU process): model sessions, KV cache, kernel selection, quantized kernels, IO queues.
  - Autoscaler & Capacity Manager: scales worker pools and enforces reserved capacity for Dedicated customers.
  - Observability and Tracing: per-token instrumentation, request traces, and cost/latency breakdowns.

- Key design choices:
  - Continuous batching: maximize utilization for bursty workloads while honoring per-request latency SLOs.
  - Kernel selection layer: model-architecture + sequence-length aware selection of optimized kernels at runtime.
  - Multi-variant model support: automatically route to quantized or lower-cost variants when capacity constrained.
  - KV-prefix caching: shared prefix cache per model version to reduce time for repeated prompts.

2. Kernel scheduling design

Goals:
- Maximize GPU throughput and utilization.
- Meet per-request P99 latency SLOs (see SLOs table below).
- Avoid head-of-line blocking from large, long-sequence requests.

Policy primitives:
- Priority classes: latency-sensitive (high), standard (medium), batchable (low).
- Dynamic slot allocation: each GPU exposes N slots; scheduler maps batches to slots considering model memory and KV-cache size.
- Preemption: long-running low-priority batches may be preempted when high-priority traffic arrives; preemption is cooperative via checkpointed KV states.
- Packing heuristics: group requests by sequence length and model variant to reduce wasted compute.

Configuration (example):

| Parameter                 | Default | Notes |
|--------------------------|---------|-------|
| gpu_slots_per_device     | "8"     | Number of concurrent slots per A100/80GB-equivalent device |
| max_batch_tokens         | "131072"| Max sum of tokens in a batch to avoid OOM |
| preemption_threshold_ms  | "200"   | If high-priority request waits > threshold, preempt low-priority batch |
| packing_sequence_tolerance | "16"  | Allow +/- tokens when packing by sequence length |

Operational knobs (CLI examples):
- To adjust slot count: ./runtime-admin set-config --key gpu_slots_per_device --value 6 --env prod
- To toggle preemption: ./runtime-admin set-config --key preemption_enabled --value false --env prod

3. Profiling playbook (profiling for performance regressions)

When to profile:
- New kernel/optimization merge into main targeting runtime
- Regression alert from Canary/Prod (token latency increase > 10% P95 or 15% P99 vs baseline)
- Customer-reported latency spike tied to specific model/version

Steps:
1. Reproduce the workload: capture representative requests using the tracing UI or run the capture tool: ./capture-workload --duration 10m --route /v1/generate --out /tmp/workload.json
2. Run microbenchmark locally on a dev instance matching target GPU: ./benchmark --gpu a100-80 --model my-model --seq-length 2048 --batch 4 --profile --out /tmp/profile.json
3. Collect traces and flamegraphs: use collector: ./trace-collect --input /tmp/profile.json --format flamegraph.svg
4. Compare kernel timelines to baseline (stored in S3 at s3://redwood-runtime-baselines/): ./compare-profiles --baseline s3://... --candidate /tmp/profile.json
5. If regression confirmed, roll back the kernel change via canary rollback and open an ADR: ./deploy rollback --canary-id <id>

Profiling metrics to capture:
- forward_token_latency_ms (per-token P50/P95/P99)
- kernel_exec_time_ms (per kernel)
- GPU_utilization_pct (avg, 95th)
- memory_allocations_mb and peak_memory_mb
- batch_compaction_rate (how often packing reduces CPU-to-GPU copies)

4. Benchmarking suite (how we measure performance)

Scope:
- Microbenchmarks: kernel-level latency and throughput across sequence lengths and batch sizes.
- Macrobenchmarks: full end-to-end request latency and tokens/sec for representative routes (chat, streaming, embeddings).
- Cost-per-token simulation: estimate $/k tokens using observed throughput and cloud GPU compute rates.

Standard scenarios to run weekly in CI:
- short-context generation: seq=64, batch=16, variant=fp16
- medium-context generation: seq=512, batch=8, variant=int8
- long-context generation: seq=8192, batch=1, variant=int8 with KV cache warm
- streaming chat (latency-first): target P95 < 150ms token for short-context flows

Automation examples (CI job):
- pipeline: tests/runtime/benchmarks.yml runs on release branch; outputs stored in artifacts and compared to baseline.
- alert: if any macrobench P95 increases > 12% vs baseline, fail CI and create issue in runtime-performance board.

5. Release notes (recent notable changes)

- 2026-02-20: Kernel selector v2.1 deployed to canary — better packing heuristics for long sequences, avg throughput +10% for seq 2048 workloads.
- 2026-02-24: Add cooperative preemption to reduce latency tail for high-priority requests; default enabled in prod.
- 2026-02-27: Int8 quantized attention kernel swapped for fallback provider for models with rotary embeddings to fix numerical drift (see known issues).

6. Known issues and mitigations

- Issue: Int8 attention numerical drift for models with rotary embeddings (detected in internal evals).
  - Impact: minor token-level divergence for some prompt patterns; observed in <0.5% of samples.
  - Mitigation: fallback to fp16 attention kernel for affected model families until targeted fix is available.
  - Workaround: In model-onboarding, tag affected models with label "rotary-int8-fallback" to auto-select fallback kernel.

- Issue: OOM with very wide-batch + long-seq combinations on older GPU SKUs (V100-class).
  - Impact: occasional worker crashes during large-scale stress tests.
  - Mitigation: autoscaler policy sets conservative gpu_slots_per_device for legacy SKUs; runtime rejects requests exceeding device_profile.max_seq_by_slots.

- Issue: Canary-to-prod rollout occasionally leaves stale cache entries causing 1-2% latency spikes.
  - Mitigation: rollout script now includes cache-invalidate step: ./deploy canary --invalidate-cache true

7. Operational runbooks (on-call procedures)

P1: Production latency degradation (alerts: P99 tokens latency > SLO * 1.5 or cascading errors)
1. Triage: Check dashboards (per-route P95/P99, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth). Owner: on-call runtime engineer.
2. Isolate: Identify affected route(s) and model versions. Use trace sampling to find problematic kernels.
3. Quick fix options (ordered by low impact to high):
   a. Toggle fallback to lower-concurrency kernels: ./runtime-admin set-config --key kernel_selector_mode --value conservative
   b. Scale up workers for affected region: ./autoscaler scale --pool runtime-prod-us-west --delta 4
   c. Temporarily route traffic to dedicated capacity or alternative region: ./router route --from us-west --to us-east --route /v1/generate --percentage 30
4. If root cause is a recent deploy, rollback canary: ./deploy rollback --canary-id <id>
5. Post-incident: Run profiling playbook and open a postmortem in confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems.

P2: Worker OOM / GPU crash
1. Check worker logs and dmesg for OOM kills. Gather last request id and captured workload if available.
2. Restart affected worker: kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-worker-<node-pool> -n runtime-prod
3. If crash persists, scale down gpu_slots_per_device and restart: ./runtime-admin set-config --key gpu_slots_per_device --value 4 --env prod
4. If related to model variant, tag and quarantine model: ./model-registry tag --model-id <id> --tag quarantined --reason "OOM"

8. Team wiki and onboarding notes

- Owner directories: serving-runtime team wiki includes design docs, ADRs, and kernel provider contracts. Owner: Marco Diaz.
- Onboarding checklist for new runtime engineers:
  1. Read this document and serving-runtime-architecture-playbook-2026.
  2. Run through the profiling playbook and submit at least one microbenchmark result.
  3. Shadow on-call for two weeks.
  4. Complete runbook drill: simulate a canary rollback and cache invalidation in staging.

10. Appendix: SLOs and thresholds

| Metric                          | Target (prod) |
|---------------------------------|---------------|
| short-context P95 token latency | "< 120ms"     |
| short-context P99 token latency | "< 220ms"     |
| medium-context P95 token latency| "< 250ms"     |
| token-availability (errors)     | "< 0.1%"      |
| worker uptime                   | "99.95%"      |
